title: Holistic prompt ledger and temporal slot sharing for cross-request KV reuse
creator: Anika Patel
description: Prototype and implement a lightweight 'prompt ledger' + temporal slot sharing layer that increases prefix KV reuse across interleaved requests while bounding GPU memory overhead and controlling p99 latency impact. The goal is to reconcile similar prompt prefixes across tenants/requests using a compact fingerprint ledger, opportunistic slot sharing for GPU slabs, and an eviction policy that considers temporal locality and request-slot affinity. This ticket covers design, bench prototype, integration with the serving runtime's slab allocator, and rollout plan including monitoring and fallback thresholds.
comments: 2025-11-21 - Kickoff: scoped to inference paths for short conversational prefixes (<= 256 tokens). Decided to focus on CPU-resident metadata with GPU slab references to avoid copying large structures into host memory.

2025-11-24 - Spike results: prototype ledger using 64-bit simhash-like fingerprint reduced unique prefixes by ~18% on sample internal traffic (dev-staging trace). Memory overhead of ledger ~2.4MB per 10k entries. Luis to iterate on false-positive tuning.

2025-11-28 - Design review (PM + Runtime): agreed that ledger entries are immutable with TTL and version tags to allow model rollouts. Need a safety cutoff to avoid serving stale cached kv for model updates. PM requested an explicit rollback plan for regressions in generation quality.

2025-11-30 - Engineering note: integrated temporal slot sharing into the slab allocator abstraction; added a soft-credit system so multiple prefixes can point to a shared slab slot if their KV fingerprints are compatible. Initial microbench shows p50 latency +1.8ms, p99 +9ms with heavy dedupe — tradeoff acceptable for unlocked cost savings in Dedicated customers.

2025-12-03 - Feedback from QA: observed a small increase in token mismatch for prompts with structured slots (function-calling prompts). Decided to add a structure-aware fingerprint pass to avoid merging prompts that differ in invocation schema.

2025-12-05 - Plan updated: add canary rollout gating (10% traffic) and metric alerts (cache_hit_rate, token_quality_regressions, p99_latency_delta). Create two toggles: ledger_enabled and slot_sharing_enabled so we can enable/disable independently.
2025-12-05 - Linked PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891 (WIP) — implements ledger API, fingerprinting, and a test harness for retention/eviction correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype passes unit tests for correctness across model version changes (no stale KV usage after model switch).
Integration benchmark demonstrates >=10% reduction in GPU-resident KV entries for mixed conversational workload without increasing p99 latency more than 12ms on average compared to baseline.
Canary rollout plan documented and automated with feature flags; rollback path validated in staging.
Observability dashboards created for ledger size, dedupe_rate, cache_hit_rate_by_tenant, p99_latency_delta, and token_quality_alerts.
Security review confirms ledger metadata contains no customer PII and KMS/HSM ownership not required for the ledger itself.
design_decisions: Keep ledger metadata CPU-resident and compact (64-bit fingerprint + 16-bit affinity tag + 32-bit timestamp) to minimize GPU memory pressure.
Use two-phase fingerprinting: cheap tokenized n-gram hash for fast lookup, then content-aware fingerprint (structure-aware) for final reconciliation to reduce false merges in structured prompts.
Implement slot sharing via soft-credits: a slab slot may accept up to N compatible references; credits decay over time to prefer exclusive residency for hot prefixes.
Eviction policy combines recency (LRU-like), temporal locality (session affinity), and a similarity score to prefer keeping representative canonical slots for clusters of similar prefixes.
Expose independent feature flags (ledger_enabled, slot_sharing_enabled, structure_sensitive_fingerprint) for safe progressive rollout and A/B testing.
Fallback behavior: if ledger lookup latency exceeds threshold or similarity confidence is low, fall back to baseline per-request KV allocation.
Model rollout safety: ledger entries are namespaced by model fingerprint/version; ledger can be flushed automatically on model upgrades or selectively invalidated by configurable predicates.
benchmarks: Workload: mixed chat + single-turn prompts sampled from production dev traces (10k reqs).
Baseline: standalone per-request KV residency. Baseline GPU KV entries: 1.0x (reference).
Prototype: ledger + slot sharing reduced GPU-resident KV entries by 12% on the sample trace; dedupe_rate=0.18; heap overhead on CPU ~2.4MB/10k ledger entries.
Latency: median +1.8ms, p95 +6ms, p99 +9ms in loaded microbench. Tail impact concentrated on requests that trigger ledger reconciliation flow; econ gating via confidence threshold recommended.
Quality: initial token-quality regression observed in 0.06% of deduped cases where structure-awareness not enabled. Structure-aware fingerprint pass reduced regressions to 0.003%.
Cost projection: for a Dedicated pool with 2000 concurrent slots, estimated token cost savings of 6-9% from reduced redundant KV recomputation (workload-dependent).
risks: Incorrect merging of structured prompts can change generation outputs; mitigated by structure-sensitive fingerprint and conservative confidence threshold.
Ledger growth in long-tail tenants could increase CPU memory; mitigation: TTL, adaptive sampling, and per-tenant caps.
Rollback complexity if ledger entries are heavily shared across slots; mitigated by namespacing ledger by model version and providing targeted invalidation APIs.
Increased p99 latency for reconciliation path under heavy contention; mitigated by asynchronous prefetcher and early-exit thresholds.
